# Lisa OS — the keyboard map

**Generated by `os/repo-tools/build-keymap.py`. Do not edit.**
Run `just lint` and it regenerates; a shortcut added, removed or
rebound without this file following fails the gate.

Every row is derived from a file that binds the key, never from a
description of one. The **Bound by** column is the point: issue
#255 was a chord reserved in a comment, freed in a settings file,
named in the PLAN, and registered by nothing — which read exactly
like a working shortcut until somebody pressed it.

## Lisa's own chords

Registered by our GNOME Shell extensions. These are **defaults, not
locks**: no `locks/` directory ships, so Settings → Keyboard rebinds
any of them and the change sticks.

| Chord | What it does | Declared in | Bound by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Shift+Super+Space` | Summon or dismiss the assistant overlay | `shell/overlay-extension/schemas/org.gnome.shell.extensions.lisa-overlay.gschema.xml` | `overlay-extension/extension.js` |
| `Shift+Super+V` | Hold to talk to Lisa | `shell/overlay-extension/schemas/org.gnome.shell.extensions.lisa-overlay.gschema.xml` | `overlay-extension/extension.js` |
| `Super+C` | Open the Lisa Assistant chat window | `shell/overlay-extension/schemas/org.gnome.shell.extensions.lisa-overlay.gschema.xml` | `overlay-extension/extension.js` |
| `Super+Space` | Open the Lisa search | `shell/launcher/schemas/org.gnome.shell.extensions.lisa-launcher.gschema.xml` | `launcher/extension.js` |

## GNOME keys Lisa sets

GNOME registers these; we choose the chord, or clear it. A row with
an empty chord is a key we deliberately give back — see
`20-lisa-keys` for why the bare Super key is one of them.

| Chord | GNOME key | Set in | Bound by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Control+Super+Space` | GNOME's `switch-input-source` | `os/packages/lisa/10_lisa-shell.gschema.override` `[org.gnome.desktop.wm.keybindings]` | GNOME, via the package (Track L and the image both install it) |
| `Super+A` | GNOME's `toggle-application-view` | `os/mkosi/mkosi.extra/etc/dconf/db/local.d/20-lisa-keys` `[org/gnome/shell/keybindings]` | GNOME, via the image's dconf defaults |
| — *(deliberately empty)* | `switch-input-source-backward` is unset, so GNOME's default does not fire | `os/packages/lisa/10_lisa-shell.gschema.override` `[org.gnome.desktop.wm.keybindings]` | GNOME, via the package (Track L and the image both install it) |
| — *(deliberately empty)* | `overlay-key` is unset, so GNOME's default does not fire | `os/mkosi/mkosi.extra/etc/dconf/db/local.d/20-lisa-keys` `[org/gnome/mutter]` | GNOME, via the image's dconf defaults |

## Chords named in prose that nothing binds

None. Every chord our settings files talk about is in a table above.

## What this map cannot tell you

- **Whether the key press works.** Registering a binding needs the
  extension loaded, which needs a session. The map proves the chord
  is declared and registered, not that mutter delivered it.
- **Gestures.** Double-tap Shift (#208) is toolkit-scoped on Wayland
  and reaches fcitx5 only inside a GTK app, so it is not a system
  shortcut and has no row here.
- **What the key is called on your keyboard.** Super is ⌘ on Apple
  hardware; labelling per-layout is #256, and it should read this
  file rather than keep a second list.
